name: Clojure runtime code evaluation of dynamic strings
attack_scenario: user-input = "#=(clojure.java.shell/sh \"sh\" \"-c\" \"id\")" runs a command at read time; edn/read-string refuses reader-eval and only returns data.
negative_test_hint: feed the reader the input "#=(System/exit 0)" and assert it is parsed as inert data or rejected, never evaluated

exemplar.explanation: eval and load-string execute Clojure code, and bare read-string (unlike namespaced clojure.edn/read-string) honors *read-eval* reader macros such as #=(...), so reading attacker text is remote code execution. The read-string pattern is anchored to the bare, unqualified call, so edn/read-string is not flagged.
